_comment: Issue #389 (F-TEST-003): reviewed DNS, TLS, QUIC and HTTP/2 accuracy cases.
Checked by tools/ci/tests/check-accuracy-corpus.py; NOT part of ci/golden_pcaps.txt,
so the golden classification fingerprint's input set is unchanged.
expected counts are per packet: wire = carries the family's wire-protocol label,
other = attributed to a different application protocol, abstain = no application verdict;
attribution = application names the SDK derives heuristically beneath the wire label.
abstain counts include payload-less packets (e.g. TCP SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK), which carry no application data.

cases.description: DNS query and matching response (A accuracy.example -> 192.0.2.10) on UDP/53.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: RFC 1035 §4.1 header, question and answer RR (compression pointer 0xc00c) decoded by hand
QR/RD/RA flags and ANCOUNT=1 consistent with the answer section

cases.description: Plain ASCII text exchanged over UDP/53 in both directions; the port alone must not yield a DNS verdict.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: payload is not a parseable DNS header+question (QDCOUNT/label structure invalid)

cases.description: TCP/443 three-way handshake, TLS ClientHello (SNI accuracy.example) and ServerHello.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: RFC 5246 §7.4.1.2/§7.4.1.3 TLS 1.2 ClientHello (suites 0x002f, 0x0035) and ServerHello; record and handshake lengths consistent; SNI extension per RFC 6066 §3
SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK carry no payload: their abstention is correct, not a miss

cases.description: Same TLS exchange with SNI www.google.com: the wire protocol is TLS; the application name the SDK derives from the SNI is heuristic attribution.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: bytes identical to acc_tls_positive except the SNI host name and the lengths that depend on it
attribution (ssl.google) is reported separately and never counted as wire-protocol accuracy

cases.description: Plaintext HTTP/1.1 request and response on TCP/443; the port alone must not yield a TLS verdict.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: payload starts with an ASCII request line, not a TLS record header (content type 0x47 is invalid)
expected handling: http for the two data packets, abstention for the handshake

cases.description: QUIC v1 (RFC 9000) client and server Initial packets on UDP/443 followed by a client 1-RTT short-header packet on the same flow.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: RFC 9000 §17.2 long header: form+fixed bits, version 0x00000001, CID lengths, Initial token length, varint Length match
client Initial padded to a 1200-byte UDP payload (RFC 9000 §14.1)
RFC 9000 §17.3 short header carries the server-chosen connection ID (the server Initial's SCID) as DCID

cases.description: QUIC version 2 (RFC 9369, 0x6b3343cf) Initial exchange on UDP/443. Genuine QUIC, but the SDK recognises only version 1 (TODO #333), so the expected handling is an abstention.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: RFC 9369 §3.2 long packet type 0b01 = Initial for version 2, with Token Length field; client Initial padded to 1200 bytes
abstention is the documented, accepted handling until #333 adds v2; it is reported, not hidden

cases.description: Prior-knowledge cleartext HTTP/2 (RFC 9113 §3.3) on TCP/8080: client preface+SETTINGS+HEADERS, server SETTINGS+SETTINGS ACK.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: RFC 9113 §3.4 preface, §6.5 SETTINGS (MAX_CONCURRENT_STREAMS=100) and §6.2 HEADERS (END_STREAM|END_HEADERS) framing
HPACK block uses static-table indices 2/6/4 and a literal :authority (RFC 7541)

cases.description: HTTP/1.1 request offering an h2c upgrade that the server declines with 200 OK; the flow stays HTTP/1.1 and must not be labelled HTTP/2.

provenance.redistribution: Synthetic: every byte is produced by the generator from constants in the source tree (RFC 5737 documentation addresses, RFC 2606/6761 reserved names, locally administered MACs); no captured traffic, no third-party data. Redistributable under the repository licence.

checks: RFC 7540 §3.2 Upgrade/HTTP2-Settings headers; no 101 Switching Protocols, no preface (RFC 9113 §3.1 deprecates h2c upgrade, but clients still send it)
expected handling: http for the two data packets, abstention for the handshake
